examInfo.title: JAMB Economics 2010 Past Questions
examInfo.subject: Economics
examInfo.instructions: Choose the correct option from A-D for each question.

questions.question: Which Economics question paper type is given to you?
questions.explanation: This question identifies the paper type for administrative purposes.

questions.question: Economics is the study of human behaviour as it relates to the
questions.explanation: Economics is fundamentally concerned with how societies allocate scarce resources to satisfy unlimited wants.

questions.question: The downturn in the prices of shares on stock markets is a highlight of

options.C: the regulatory nature of the market

questions.explanation: The invisible hand concept explains how market forces naturally regulate prices, including stock market fluctuations.

questions.question: If x̄ = 6 and N = 6, determine the value of Σfx
questions.explanation: Since x̄ = Σfx/N, then Σfx = x̄ × N = 6 × 6 = 36

questions.question: The standard deviation of a set of data is
questions.explanation: Standard deviation measures how spread out data points are from the mean, making it a measure of dispersion.

questions.question: The mean is the best measure of central tendency because it

options.A: is not affected by extreme values in a data
options.B: is a midpoint value in an array of data
options.C: is a balancing point in an observation
options.D: can be calculated from incomplete data

questions.explanation: The mean acts as a balancing point where the sum of deviations above and below it equals zero.

questions.question: The most popular sizes of dresses and shoes are determined by the
questions.explanation: The mode represents the most frequently occurring value, which indicates the most popular sizes.

questions.question: If the demand for a good is more elastic than its supply, the tax burden is borne
questions.explanation: When demand is more elastic than supply, producers bear more of the tax burden because consumers are more responsive to price changes.

questions.question: If the price of a commodity with elastic demand increases, the revenue accruing to the producer will
questions.explanation: With elastic demand, the percentage decrease in quantity demanded exceeds the percentage increase in price, leading to decreased total revenue.

questions.question: An excess demand for beans will result from

options.A: an increase in the price of beans
options.B: a decrease in the price of beans
options.C: an increase in the supply of beans
options.D: a decrease in the supply of beans

questions.explanation: A decrease in price increases quantity demanded while quantity supplied decreases, creating excess demand.

questions.question: Consumer surplus tends to be higher when demand is
questions.explanation: With elastic demand, consumers are more responsive to price changes, allowing them to capture more surplus when prices are favorable.

questions.question: One of the assumptions of ordinal utility theory is that

options.C: total utility is a function of price

questions.explanation: Ordinal utility theory assumes that consumers can rank their preferences in order without measuring exact utility levels.

questions.question: The law of diminishing marginal utility explains why

options.A: the slope of a normal demand curve is negative
options.B: an abnormal demand curve slopes upwards
options.C: the slope of a normal demand curve is positive
options.D: the consumption of inferior goods increases with income

questions.explanation: As marginal utility decreases with additional consumption, consumers are willing to pay less for additional units, creating a downward-sloping demand curve.

questions.question: If a consumer plans to spend ₦120 on four oranges but spent ₦80, his consumer surplus is
questions.explanation: Consumer surplus = What consumer was willing to pay - What consumer actually paid = ₦120 - ₦80 = ₦40. Per orange = ₦40/4 = ₦10 = ₦1.00

questions.question: A set of factors that can shift the supply curve are changes in
questions.explanation: Technology, weather, and population are non-price factors that can shift the entire supply curve. Price causes movement along the curve, not a shift.

questions.question: If the coefficient of price elasticity of supply is greater than one, the supply is said to be
questions.explanation: When the coefficient of price elasticity of supply is greater than 1, supply is elastic or fairly elastic.

questions.question: If commodity X is a by-product of commodity Y, this implies that both commodities are
questions.explanation: When one commodity is a by-product of another, they are produced together, making them jointly supplied.

questions.question: In perfect competition, price is determined by the
questions.explanation: In perfect competition, price is determined by the interaction of market forces (supply and demand), not by individual participants.

questions.question: In order to reduce hardship faced by consumers due to high prices government can introduce
questions.explanation: Maximum prices (price ceilings) set below market equilibrium help reduce consumer hardship by keeping prices affordable.

questions.question: Average product is less than marginal product when

options.A: there is constant returns to scale
options.B: there is increasing returns to scale
options.C: there is decreasing returns to scale

questions.explanation: When there are increasing returns to scale, marginal product is greater than average product, pulling the average up.

questions.question: A firm enjoying economies of scale is said to be

options.A: reducing average cost as production increases
options.B: benefiting from the activities of other firms
options.D: having an upward-sloping average cost curve

questions.explanation: Economies of scale occur when average costs decrease as the scale of production increases.

questions.question: The rising portion of the long-run average cost curve of a firm is an indication that it is experiencing
questions.explanation: When the long-run average cost curve is rising, the firm is experiencing diseconomies of scale.

questions.question: An industry's supply curve is more likely to be elastic when firms are
questions.explanation: When firms operate below capacity, they can easily increase output in response to price changes, making supply more elastic.

questions.question: One of the characteristics of monopolistic competition is that

options.A: there is mobility of factors of production
options.B: no single seller dominates the market
options.D: consumers have perfect knowledge of price

questions.explanation: In monopolistic competition, there are many sellers, so no single seller can dominate the market.

questions.question: The demand curve for factors of production
questions.explanation: The demand curve for factors of production slopes downwards due to the law of diminishing marginal productivity.

questions.question: An agreement among firms on price and segmentation is termed
questions.explanation: A cartel is a formal agreement among firms to coordinate prices and market segmentation.

questions.question: In national income accounting, tax is determined by the
questions.explanation: In national income accounting, tax is typically a function of the level of income earned.

questions.question: A decrease in aggregate spending in an economy will ultimately lead to
questions.explanation: A decrease in aggregate spending reduces economic activity, leading to recession.

questions.question: If MPC is 0.7 while government expenditure increased by ₦150m, the equilibrium national income is
The function of money which makes division of labour possible is its
questions.explanation: Money as a medium of exchange facilitates trade and specialization, making division of labour possible.

questions.question: By buying treasury bills, the Central Bank of Nigeria intends to

options.A: increase money supply in the economy
options.B: reduce the cash reserve ratio for banks
options.C: reduce money supply in the economy
options.D: increase the capital base of commercial banks

questions.explanation: When the central bank buys treasury bills, it removes money from circulation, reducing money supply.

questions.question: The velocity of money is represented as
questions.explanation: Velocity of money = Nominal GDP/Money supply, showing how many times money changes hands in the economy.

questions.question: One of the functions of commercial banks is

options.A: maintaining stable price in the economy

questions.explanation: Commercial banks primarily function to accept deposits and grant loans to customers.

questions.question: A strategy for curbing unemployment is to

options.B: increase taxes and decrease government expenditure
options.C: increase government expenditure and decrease taxes
options.D: ensure even distribution of job opportunities

questions.explanation: Expansionary fiscal policy (increasing government expenditure and decreasing taxes) stimulates economic activity and reduces unemployment.

questions.question: In Nigeria, the distribution of job opportunities
questions.explanation: This question appears incomplete in the original, but deficit budgeting is often used to stimulate employment.

questions.question: National development plans in Nigeria fail mainly because of
questions.explanation: Poor implementation strategies have been identified as a major reason for the failure of development plans in Nigeria.

questions.question: The ultimate aim of agricultural policies in Nigeria is to achieve
questions.explanation: The primary goal of agricultural policies is to achieve food sufficiency and security for the population.

questions.question: Government can boost agricultural output in Nigeria primarily by
questions.explanation: Subsidies on farm inputs reduce production costs and encourage increased agricultural output.

questions.question: Localization of industries refers to the

options.A: spread of firms producing different products
options.B: siting of industries near the market
options.C: concentration of firms of an industry
options.D: siting of firms producing different products

questions.explanation: Localization of industries refers to the concentration of similar firms in a particular geographical area.

questions.question: In developing countries, governments influence the location of industries in order to

options.D: encourage industries to earn high profits

questions.explanation: Governments influence industrial location to ensure balanced regional development and spread economic benefits.

questions.question: A disadvantage of Nigeria's dependence on imported petroleum products is the

options.A: instability in the demand for the products
options.C: instability in the supply of the product

questions.explanation: Dependence on imports creates supply instability due to external factors beyond the country's control.

questions.question: The maximum number of shareholders for a limited liability company is
questions.explanation: A limited liability company can have an unlimited number of shareholders.

questions.question: The primary motive for an individual engaging in production is to
questions.explanation: The primary motive for production in a market economy is profit maximization.

questions.question: What is the population growth rate in 2003?
questions.explanation: Based on the table provided, the population growth rate calculation would yield 50%.

questions.question: The percentage of working population in 2002 is?
questions.explanation: Based on the table, the working population percentage in 2002 is 80%.

questions.question: One of the characteristics of free trade zone is

options.B: different trade policies of non-member countries
options.C: free factor mobility within the zone

questions.explanation: Free trade zones are characterized by harmonized trade policies and reduced barriers among member countries.

questions.question: If Nigeria imports vehicles from Japan the transaction will appear as a

options.A: debit on Japan's balance of payments
options.B: credit on Japan's balance of payments
options.C: credit on Nigeria's balance of trade
options.D: credit on Nigeria's balance of payment

questions.explanation: Japan's export to Nigeria appears as a credit (positive) entry on Japan's balance of payments.

questions.question: One of the objectives of ADB is to

options.A: provide subsidies on imported goods to member countries
options.B: mobilize short-term loans for member countries
options.C: promote economic and social development of member countries
options.D: provide technical assistance to only poor member countries

questions.explanation: The African Development Bank's primary objective is to promote economic and social development of member countries.

questions.question: The choice of the method of production in an economy is determined by the
questions.explanation: The method of production is primarily determined by the level of technical knowledge and technology available.

questions.question: The amount of labour hired depends on the
questions.explanation: Firms hire labour up to the point where the marginal productivity of labour equals the wage rate.
